chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Khalid ibn Jarir, on the authority of Abil Rabi'a ash-Shamy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He (the Imam) said: 'He was asked about chess and backgammon. He said: Do not approach them.' I asked: 'What about singing/music?' He said: 'There is no good in it; do not do it.' I asked: 'What about date wine (nabidh)?' He said: 'The Messenger of God forbade every intoxicant, and every intoxicant is forbidden.' I asked: 'What about the vessels in which it is made?' He said: 'The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the Daba, al-Muzaffat, al-Hantam, and al-Naqir.' I asked: 'What are those?' He said: 'The Daba is the squash skin, and the Muzaffat is the potter's vat, and the Hantam is the grey-colored jars, and the Naqir is a wooden vessel which the people of the Age of Ignorance would hollow out until it had cavities, and they would pour wine in it.' And it has been said that the Hantam refers to the green jars.'

key_terms.الدَّبَاء: A vessel made from a hollowed-out gourd/squash
key_terms.الْمُزَفَّت: A potter's vat coated with pitch

ai.seo_question: What are the specific vessels and items forbidden in Shia jurisprudence regarding wine and intoxicants?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the prohibition of chess and backgammon is linked to their role in distracting from remembrance of God, while the ruling on singing emphasizes a lack of spiritual benefit rather than absolute invalidity. The discussion on vessels (Daba, Muzaffat, Hantam, Naqir) highlights the Shia scholarly focus on the material and method of fermentation in determining the permissibility of wine, connecting specific Prophetic traditions to the broader Quranic principle of 'Kullu muskiran haram'.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-119 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Khalid ibn Jarir, on the authority of Abil Rabi’a ash-Shamy,

“I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) about chess and backgammon. He (MGB)said, ‘God’s Prophet (MGB) said, Do not play them.’ I asked, ‘What about listening to songs?’ He (MGB) said, ‘There is no use in it. Do not listen to them.’ I asked, ‘What about drinking date wine?’ He (MGB) replied, ‘God’s Prophet (MGB) has forbidden drinking any intoxicator. All that is intoxicating is forbidden.’I asked, ‘What about using the dishes in which wine is made?’ He (MGB) replied, ‘God’s Prophet (MGB) has forbidden four kinds of them which are: Daba, Mazqat, Hantam and Naqir.’ I asked, ‘What are these?’ He (MGB) replied, ‘Daba refers to squash skin. Mazqat refers the potter’s vat. Hantam refers to grey colored pots and Naqir refers a wooden dish which was carved out until its middle became empty during the Age of Ignorance and they filled it with dates. Some have said that Hantam refers to green pots.’”
